stem: Sudden onset paralytic strabismus in a child should be regarded as what?

options.text: A condition the child will eventually grow out of
A harmless squint that needs no assessment

explanation: A medical emergency: sudden paralytic strabismus may indicate serious underlying pathology such as trauma, tumour, or raised intracranial pressure and needs urgent assessment.
rationale: Paralytic strabismus is not a benign developmental variant when it has a sudden onset.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because sudden paralytic strabismus can reflect serious underlying causes such as trauma, tumour, or raised intracranial pressure, so urgent assessment is required.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because sudden onset eye deviation is not a normal developmental phase and should not be assumed to be benign.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because longsightedness is associated with accommodative esotropia, which is different from sudden paralytic strabismus.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because a child should not simply be expected to grow out of sudden paralytic strabismus.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because a new paralytic squint is not harmless and requires prompt medical review.

source.hint: Recall how the author describes the urgency of a new, sudden loss of eye movement.
